name: Hire a Famous Boss!

pick.label: Pick a boss
pick.heading: Pick a famous boss and put them in charge
lead: Everybody has an opinion about what makes a good boss. So let’s test it. Take a famous leader (real or invented, from sport, TV, film or the kitchen) and put them in charge of something they have no business running.
Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. Some of these people would be brilliant managers. Some would be a disaster. *Your job is to imagine which.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious management theory here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some bosses make total sense, and some only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: Which famous leader are you hiring?
I’m putting them in charge of:
A Späti, a football team, your flatshare, the university canteen, a whole country…
Strict? Inspiring? Chaotic? Do they tell people what to do, or ask them first?
Why does the team end up loving them, or at least respecting them?

values.team: My old flatshare in Friedrichshain: four people, one kitchen, zero clean spoons.
values.style: Firm but kind. Practically perfect in every way, and she knows it. She never explains herself, which is annoying, but she’s always right, which is worse.
values.rule: Every chore must have an element of fun. The washing-up now has a song. It has its own WhatsApp group, and nobody is allowed to leave.
values.wrong: Jonas refuses to sing. He says he is an adult with a job in IT. Mary Poppins gives him the small room with no window.
values.works: After a week the kitchen is spotless, the fridge has a rota and somebody has bought a plant. Nobody knows who. Nobody dares to ask.

yours.label: Your boss
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your new boss in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which boss gets the job?
rank.placeholder: The boss, e.g. Mary Poppins runs the flatshare
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their new boss in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
